module.eks_blueprints.module.emr_on_eks:resource.null_resource.update_trust_policy: explicit depends_on of module.eks_blueprints.module.emr_on_eks:resource.kubernetes_namespace.spark is redundant — already implied by attribute references

module.eks_blueprints.module.aws_eks_managed_node_groups:resource.aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng: explicit depends_on of module.eks_blueprints.module.aws_eks_managed_node_groups:resource.aws_iam_role.managed_ng is redundant — already implied by attribute references

module.eks_blueprints.module.aws_eks_self_managed_node_groups:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.self_managed_ng: explicit depends_on of module.eks_blueprints.module.aws_eks_self_managed_node_groups:resource.aws_iam_instance_profile.self_managed_ng is redundant — already implied by attribute references

module.eks_blueprints.module.aws_eks_self_managed_node_groups:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.self_managed_ng: explicit depends_on of module.eks_blueprints.module.aws_eks_self_managed_node_groups:resource.aws_iam_role.self_managed_ng is redundant — already implied by attribute references

module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons installs Helm releases and Kubernetes resources via the helm/kubernetes providers, but only references the cluster's endpoint/id outputs. It has no dependency on the EKS cluster readiness gate (data.http.eks_cluster_readiness inside module.eks_blueprints) or the aws-auth ConfigMap, so on a fresh apply the add-ons can attempt to talk to the Kubernetes API before the control plane is ready or before worker identity is registered. Ordering the add-on module after the aws-auth ConfigMap (which itself waits on cluster readiness) closes this operational gap.

The explicit depends_on on aws_iam_role.managed_ng is redundant: the node group already references aws_iam_role.managed_ng[0].arn in its node_role_arn attribute, so Terraform infers the dependency automatically. (The explicit depends_on on aws_iam_instance_profile.managed_ng and aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.managed_ng is NOT redundant and should be kept, since those are needed for IAM propagation.)

The explicit depends_on on aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution is redundant: the null_resource's local-exec command already interpolates aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution.id, so the dependency is established implicitly.

The explicit depends_on on kubernetes_namespace.spark is redundant: the null_resource's local-exec command already interpolates kubernetes_namespace.spark.id, so the dependency is established implicitly.

module.aws_eks_teams creates Kubernetes namespaces, RBAC objects, and IRSA service accounts via the kubernetes provider, but has no readiness ordering: the managed/self-managed node group modules explicitly depends_on kubernetes_config_map.aws_auth (which transitively waits for EKS API readiness via data.http.eks_cluster_readiness), while the teams module does not. It can therefore race cluster bring-up and fail to create its Kubernetes resources on first apply.
